title: Why galaxies go quiet
text: Astronomers have long wondered why some galaxies stop forming new stars while others remain active for billions of years. Recent observations suggest that a supermassive black hole at the centre of a galaxy can heat the surrounding gas, preventing it from cooling and collapsing into new stars. This process, known as feedback, may explain why the largest galaxies in the universe often appear old and quiet.

title: Reconstructing memory
text: Memory is not a perfect recording of past events. Each time we recall an experience, the brain reconstructs it, and small details can change in the process. Psychologists have shown that simply wording a question differently can alter what witnesses report remembering. For this reason, researchers recommend that interviews with witnesses use open questions and avoid suggesting particular answers.

title: Locating earthquakes
text: Earthquakes occur when stress that has built up along a fault is suddenly released. Most of this energy travels through the ground as seismic waves, which scientists measure using sensitive instruments called seismometers. By comparing the arrival times of different waves at several stations, geologists can locate the source of an earthquake within minutes, allowing emergency services to respond more quickly.
